summary:
An opinion piece for Workplace Insight arguing that organisations getting real returns from agentic AI are investing in employee capability rather than cutting headcount. Framed around the launch of the UK Government's AI Skills Compact, the author (writing on behalf of Top Employers Institute) says policymakers and business leaders are shifting from viewing AI purely as an efficiency or headcount-reduction play toward equipping people to work alongside it.

Key argument one: people, not technology, drive AI ROI. The piece cites Gartner research indicating fewer than 40 percent of early AI adopter organisations have realised significant productivity gains, attributing underperformance to layering new tools onto existing ways of working without redesigning how work is organised, plus employee resistance. It also references reports of companies that laid off staff because of AI and were then forced to re-hire. Resistance, the author says, is rarely about the technology but about uncertainty over changing roles, expectations and career paths. Top Employers Institute research is said to show the strongest performers build trust and clarity, involve employees in conversations about how AI changes their work, continuously evaluate impact on both performance and employee experience, and position HR as a strategic enabler rather than a post-deployment support function.

Key argument two: democratising AI access. Vodacom Group is cited as training employees across functions to build and deploy AI solutions on low-code and no-code platforms within clear governance frameworks, producing an internal community that has delivered hundreds of new processes and measurable financial benefits.

Key argument three: freeing managers. Agentic AI, defined as intelligent systems coordinating complex workflows with minimal human intervention, can absorb repetitive admin, reporting and operational coordination, leaving managers time for coaching, talent development and culture, which the author links to profitability, retention and reduced talent loss. Yum China is cited as embedding AI across recruitment, training and operational support.

claims.claim: Fewer than 40 percent of organisations that were early adopters of AI have realised significant productivity gains from AI implementation
claims.attribution: Gartner research, as cited in the article

claims.claim: Numerous companies that laid off employees due to AI have been forced to re-hire that workforce
Organisations achieving the strongest returns from agentic AI invest as heavily in employee capability, workforce redesign and organisational readiness as in the AI technology itself
Vodacom Group's internal community of employees trained to develop automation and AI solutions has delivered hundreds of new processes and measurable financial benefits
Yum China has embedded AI across recruitment, training and operational support so managers can focus on coaching teams and employee experience
claims.attribution: Article, describing Top Employer Yum China

claims.claim: AI programmes underperform because organisations layered new tools onto existing ways of working without redesigning how work is organised, prompting employee resistance
